name: gitea-ai-usage-guardrail
description: Standing instruction - flag Gitea-repo requests that risk grade/Honor Code trouble, only for that project
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Carson asked 2026-09-03: for [[csci-435-gitea-project]] specifically, before doing something he
asks (or before handing him ready-to-use text/code), check it against [[gitea-ai-honor-code-rules]].
If a request would likely cross one of those lines, say so briefly and either propose a safer
rephrasing or let him decide - don't just silently comply, and don't refuse outright either (these
are grading-process risks, not something to gatekeep hard on).

**Concretely, flag rather than silently doing it when asked to, e.g.:**
- Write a PR description, issue reply, or reviewer-question answer that reads as final/ready to
  post verbatim, with no prompt to review or edit it first.
- Implement an issue Carson opened himself (should be someone else's, per D5).
- Skip straight to using AI to locate/understand code for an issue before he's looked himself
  (concept location must come first).
- Skip or postpone AI-log capture for a session doing real project work.
- Draft an "AI Assistance" issue/PR comment that mischaracterizes what AI did (or skip posting one).
- Anything implying shared account access with a teammate.

**Why:** Syllabus §16 makes "prompt → copy → paste" without review an Honor Code violation, and
several Sprint 0 D5 rules (concept-location-first, must-explain-every-line, no AI replies on your
own issue/PR) are graded process, not just suggestions. Carson wants a heads-up before he
accidentally does something in that gray zone, not after.

**How to apply:** Scope this to Gitea/CSCI 435 work ONLY - do not extend this caution to his other
coursework or general use, and don't be preachy about it: one short flag + an alternative or a
question, then proceed with whatever he decides. This does not change [[gitea-commit-trailers]] or
[[gitea-ai-log-gathering-workflow]], which already stand as settled.

name: gitea-wsync-test-workflow
description: Edit code in this Windows Gitea folder; run tests/lint/build in WSL Debian ~/gitea via `wsync <cmd>` from Git Bash
metadata:
  type: project
---

Carson's setup (2026-09-14): **all code edits happen in this Windows `Gitea` folder** (logged
SpecStory sessions launch here). WSL Debian `~/gitea` is a **test runner only** — never edit there.
Native Windows test runs produce Windows-only failures, and lint is ~20x slower, so don't trust them.

**Run tests/lint/build with `wsync` from the Bash tool (Git Bash):**
```bash
wsync pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/features/common-page.test.ts
wsync go test -run '^TestName$' ./routers/web/misc/
wsync make lint-js
wsync make build
wsync            # sync only
```
`C:\Users\carso\bin\wsync` reads the branch checked out here, warns if tracked files are
uncommitted (only COMMITTED work reaches WSL — commit first, ask Carson before committing), then
runs WSL `~/bin/wsync-wsl <branch> [cmd]`: fetches remote `win` (this folder over /mnt/c;
push disabled), force-switches `~/gitea` to that branch, runs the command with Go 1.26.4/Node PATH.

Gotchas: don't run `git status` on `/mnt/c` from WSL (hangs); WSL can't run `.exe`s; use
`wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c '...' name args` (plain `wsl -- bash -c` drops args).
To try the app: `~/gitea/custom/conf/app.ini` serves Gitea on http://localhost:3001 (SQLite) —
run `wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c 'cd ~/gitea && ./gitea web'` in the background after `wsync make build`.
Baseline rule: some backend tests fail on `main` too — compare branch vs `main`, not vs zero.

name: gitea-commit-trailers
description: Standing rule — in the CSCI 435 Gitea repo, never use Co-Authored-By; use Assisted-by only
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

In [[csci-435-gitea-project]], commit messages must **never** contain `Co-Authored-By` or
`Signed-off-by`. Use only:

```
Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5
```

Carson explicitly reaffirmed this on 2026-09-02 after being shown the conflict, so treat it as
settled — do not re-raise it or ask again.

**Why:** the repo's `AGENTS.md` (loaded via its `CLAUDE.md`, which is just `@AGENTS.md`) requires the
`Assisted-by` trailer and forbids the other two — sign-off must be done by a human. This directly
contradicts Claude Code's default session attribution, which appends `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...`
plus a `Claude-Session:` URL. The repo rule wins here; graders read these commits.

**How to apply:** when committing anywhere under the `Software Engineering\Gitea` tree, drop the
default attribution block entirely and write the `Assisted-by:` trailer instead. Applies to PR
descriptions too — no `Co-Authored-By` there either.

{"assignees":[{"id":"U_kgDOCJeTNQ","login":"CarsonRackley","name":"","databaseId":144151349}],"author":{"id":"U_kgDOCJeTNQ","is_bot":false,"login":"CarsonRackley","name":""},"body":"Part of #7.\n\n### User Story\n\nAs a user with many notifications, I want to select several notifications and mark them read, unread, pinned or delete them in one action so that I can triage my inbox quickly instead of clicking each notification one by one.\n\n### User Scenario\n\nSam comes back from a week away to 120 unread notifications. On the Notifications page Sam ticks the checkboxes next to 15 bot-generated notifications and clicks \"Mark as read\", and they all move to the Read tab at once. Sam then uses the \"select all\" checkbox in the header to select everything in the current view and marks it as read. Sam ticks a few notifications on page 1, goes to page 2, and ticks more; the page-1 selections are still there. Sam deletes those 21 old notifications for archived projects. A confirmation shows how many notifications were changed or deleted.\n\n### Acceptance Criteria\n\n- [ ] AC1: Given the notification list, when the user ticks individual checkboxes, then a bulk action bar appears showing the number selected, with \"Mark as read\", \"Mark as unread\", \"Pin\" and \"Delete\" actions.\n- [ ] AC2: Given N notifications are selected, when the user clicks \"Mark as read\", then exactly those N notifications change to read in one request, and no others change.\n- [ ] AC3: Given the user clicks the header \"select all\" checkbox, when an action is applied, then it affects only the notifications in the **active view** (the current tab, and any active filter), per the Design Decision below.\n- [ ] AC4: Given a bulk request that includes a notification ID belonging to another user, when the server processes it, then that notification is not changed and no information about it is returned.\n- [ ] AC5: Given nothing is selected, when the page is shown, then the bulk action buttons are hidden or disabled.\n- [ ] AC6: Given a bulk action completes, when the page updates, then the list and the navbar unread count show the new state without a manual reload.\n- [ ] AC7: Given N notifications are selected, when the user clicks \"Delete\" and confirms the prompt, then exactly those N notifications are removed from both the Unread and Read tabs, and the count shown matches N.\n- [ ] AC8: Given a deleted notification's issue or pull request gets new activity, when notifications are generated, then the user receives a fresh notification for it as normal (delete does not unsubscribe).\n- [ ] AC9: Given the user selects notifications on one page, when they move to another page of the same view, then the earlier selections are kept and the bulk action bar shows the total selected across pages.\n- [ ] AC10: Given selections exist, when the user switches tab, changes a filter, or completes a bulk action, then all selections are cleared.\n\n### Out of Scope\n\n- Adding new filters. The \"view\" is the active tab plus the repository and type filters from #50.\n- Unsubscribing from the underlying issue or pull request as part of delete.\n- Keyboard shortcuts for selection.\n- Changes to the notifications API.\n\n### Open Questions\n\n- The page already has \"Mark all as read\". Should that stay as a separate button, or become \"select all + Mark as read\"? (Proposed: Stay separate)\n\n### Design Decision\n\n#### Decision 1: What \"select all\" selects\n\n**Decision:** \"Select all\" selects the notifications visible on the current page of the active view. When more notifications match the view, a link offers \"Select all N notifications in this view\". Bulk actions never reach outside the active view.\n**Alternatives Considered:** (1) \"Select all\" means every notification the user has, ignoring the active tab and filters. (2) \"Select all\" is limited to the visible page, with no way to extend it.\n**Rationale:** Option 1 is surprising and destructive: it can change hundreds of notifications the user can't see. Option 2 is safe but forces the user to page through everything. Starting from the visible page, with an explicit opt-in to extend, matches how GitHub and Gmail behave.\n**Consequences:** For \"all N in this view\", the server re-applies the view's criteria rather than trusting a list of IDs from the browser. Every ID in a bulk request must be checked against the signed-in user. When #50 lands, its query parameters join the view criteria automatically.\n**Pinned notifications:** Pinned notifications are part of every view, since they appear in both tabs. \"Select all N\" counts and acts on them too. Because pinned is a status rather than a flag, bulk \"Mark as read\" or \"Mark as unread\" unpins them, matching the existing single-notification button.\n\n#### Decision 2: Selections persist across pages of the same view\n\n**Decision:** Keep selected notification IDs in the browser's session storage, keyed by the view (tab plus filters), so they survive moving between pages. Clear them when the view changes or a bulk action completes.\n**Alternatives Considered:** (1) Reset selections on every page load. (2) Carry selected IDs in the URL query string. (3) Store selections on the server.\n**Rationale:** Resetting makes it impossible to hand-pick notifications across pages, which is the main case \"select all N\" doesn't cover. URLs get long and unwieldy with many IDs. Storing on the server adds a table or session state for what is purely temporary UI state. Session storage is per tab, needs no backend change, and ends with the tab.\n**Consequences:** The bulk action bar must show the total selected across pages, not just the visible ones (AC9). Clearing on a view change (AC10) prevents acting on items that no longer match what the user sees. Selections don't carry over to a new tab. Since the IDs come from the browser, the server still checks that each one belongs to the user (AC4).\n\n#### Decision 3: Delete is a hard delete, behind a confirmation\n\n**Decision:** \"Delete\" removes the notification rows for the signed-in user after a confirmation prompt. Deleting does not unsubscribe the user from the underlying issue or pull request.\n**Alternatives Considered:** (1) A soft \"done\" status that hides the row but keeps it. (2) Delete without confirmation, plus an undo toast.\n**Rationale:** Gitea already recreates or updates the notification row when new activity happens, so a hard delete behaves like \"done\" without a new status value or schema change (AC8). Undo would need the deleted rows kept somewhere temporarily. A confirmation prompt is simpler and matches other destructive actions in Gitea.\n**Consequences:** Gitea has no per-notification delete today, so this adds a new server route, not just a new button. Deleted notifications can't be recovered. If the sprint runs short, delete is the most independent part of this issue and can be split into its own issue without affecting Decisions 1 and 2.\n\n### Scope\n\nmedium\n\n---\nDrafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5); Reviewed and changed by Carson.\n\n","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAACtk8WWQ","name":"enhancement","description":"New feature or request","color":"a2eeef"},{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAAC0JZx6A","name":"scope: medium","description":"","color":"1545a8"}],"milestone":{"number":1,"title":"Sprint 1","description":"","dueOn":"2026-10-08T00:00:00Z"},"state":"OPEN","title":"Bulk actions on notifications (mark read/unread, pin, delete)"}

    42	// Notifications is the notification list page
    43	func Notifications(ctx *context.Context) {
    44		prepareUserNotificationsData(ctx)
    45		if ctx.Written() {
    46			return
    47		}
    48		if ctx.FormBool("div-only") {
    49			ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplNotificationDiv)
    50			return
    51		}
    52		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplNotification)
    53	}
    54	
    55	func prepareUserNotificationsData(ctx *context.Context) {
    56		pageType := ctx.FormString("type", ctx.FormString("q")) // "q" is the legacy query parameter for "page type"
    57		page := max(1, ctx.FormInt("page"))
    58		perPage := util.IfZero(ctx.FormInt("perPage"), 20) // this value is never used or exposed ....
    59		queryStatus := util.Iif(pageType == "read", activities_model.NotificationStatusRead, activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread)
    60		filter := parseNotificationFilter(ctx)
    61	
    62		countOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID)
    63		countOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{queryStatus}
    64		total, err := db.Count[activities_model.Notification](ctx, countOpts)
    65		if err != nil {
    66			ctx.ServerError("ErrGetNotificationCount", err)
    67			return
    68		}
    69	
    70		unreadOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID)
    71		unreadOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread}
    72		filteredUnreadCount, err := db.Count[activities_model.Notification](ctx, unreadOpts) // the navbar badge stays global
    73		if err != nil {
    74			ctx.ServerError("ErrGetNotificationCount", err)
    75			return
    76		}
    77	
    78		filterRepos, unreadRepoIDs, err := loadNotificationFilterRepos(ctx, ctx.Doer)
    79		if err != nil {
    80			ctx.ServerError("loadNotificationFilterRepos", err)
    81			return
    82		}
    83	
    84		pager := context.NewPagination(total, perPage, page, 5)
    85		if pager.Paginater.Current() < page {
    86			// use the last page if the requested page is more than total pages
    87			page = pager.Paginater.Current()
    88			pager = context.NewPagination(total, perPage, page, 5)
    89		}
    90	
    91		findOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID) // pinned rows are filtered like the rest
    92		findOpts.ListOptions = db.ListOptions{
    93			PageSize: perPage,
    94			Page:     page,
    95		}
    96		findOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{queryStatus, activities_model.NotificationStatusPinned}
    97		nls, err := db.Find[activities_model.Notification](ctx, findOpts)
    98		if err != nil {
    99			ctx.ServerError("db.Find[activities_model.Notification]", err)
   100			return
   101		}
   102	
   103		notifications := activities_model.NotificationList(nls)
   104	
   105		failCount := 0
   106	
   107		repos, failures, err := notifications.LoadRepos(ctx)
   108		if err != nil {
   109			ctx.ServerError("LoadRepos", err)
   110			return
   111		}
   112		notifications = notifications.Without(failures)
   113		if err := repos.LoadAttributes(ctx); err != nil {
   114			ctx.ServerError("LoadAttributes", err)
   115			return
   116		}
   117		failCount += len(failures)
   118		notifications, failures, err = filterNotificationsByRepoAccess(ctx, ctx.Doer, notifications)
   119		if err != nil {
   120			ctx.ServerError("filterNotificationsByRepoAccess", err)
   121			return
   122		}
   123		failCount += len(failures)
   124	
   125		failures, err = notifications.LoadIssues(ctx)
   126		if err != nil {
   127			ctx.ServerError("LoadIssues", err)
   128			return
   129		}
   130	
   131		if err = notifications.LoadIssuePullRequests(ctx); err != nil {
   132			ctx.ServerError("LoadIssuePullRequests", err)
   133			return
   134		}
   135	
   136		notifications = notifications.Without(failures)
   137		failCount += len(failures)
   138	
   139		failures, err = notifications.LoadComments(ctx)
   140		if err != nil {
   141			ctx.ServerError("LoadComments", err)
   142			return
   143		}
   144		notifications = notifications.Without(failures)
   145		failCount += len(failures)
   146	
   147		if failCount > 0 {
   148			ctx.Flash.Error(fmt.Sprintf("ERROR: %d notifications were removed due to missing parts - check the logs", failCount))
   149		}
   150	
   151		ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("notifications")
   152		ctx.Data["PageType"] = pageType
   153		ctx.Data["Notifications"] = notifications
   154		ctx.Data["Link"] = setting.AppSubURL + "/notifications"
   155		ctx.Data["SequenceNumber"] = ctx.FormString("sequence-number")
   156		ctx.Data["FilterRepoID"] = filter.RepoID
   157		ctx.Data["FilterSource"] = filter.Source
   158		ctx.Data["IsFiltered"] = filter.IsActive()
   159		ctx.Data["FilterRepos"] = filterRepos
   160		ctx.Data["FilterRepoUnread"] = unreadRepoIDs
   161		ctx.Data["FilteredUnreadCount"] = filteredUnreadCount
   162		for _, repo := range filterRepos {
   163			if repo.ID == filter.RepoID {
   164				ctx.Data["FilterRepo"] = repo // only accessible repos are named, a guessed ID shows the generic label
   165				break
   166			}
   167		}
   168	
   169		pager.AddParamFromRequest(ctx.Req)
   170		pager.RemoveParam(container.SetOf("div-only", "sequence-number"))
   171		ctx.Data["Page"] = pager
   172	}
   173	
   174	func filterNotificationsByRepoAccess(ctx stdCtx.Context, doer *user_model.User, notifications activities_model.NotificationList) (activities_model.NotificationList, []int, error) {
   175		failures := make([]int, 0)
   176		for i, notification := range notifications {
   177			if notification.Repository == nil {
   178				continue
   179			}
   180			perm, err := access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx, notification.Repository, doer)
   181			if err != nil {
   182				return nil, nil, err
   183			}
   184			if !perm.HasAnyUnitAccessOrPublicAccess() {
   185				failures = append(failures, i)
   186			}
   187		}
   188		return notifications.Without(failures), failures, nil
   189	}
   190	
   191	// notificationSourceParams maps the "source" query value to the notification source it selects
   192	var notificationSourceParams = map[string]activities_model.NotificationSource{
   193		"issue":      activities_model.NotificationSourceIssue,
   194		"pull":       activities_model.NotificationSourcePullRequest,
   195		"commit":     activities_model.NotificationSourceCommit,
   196		"repository": activities_model.NotificationSourceRepository,
   197	}
   198	
   199	// notificationFilter is the repository and type filter of the notifications page
   200	type notificationFilter struct {
   201		RepoID int64
   202		Source string // a key of notificationSourceParams, or "" for any
   203	}
   204	
   205	func parseNotificationFilter(ctx *context.Context) notificationFilter {
   206		filter := notificationFilter{RepoID: max(0, ctx.FormInt64("repo"))}
   207		if source := ctx.FormString("source"); notificationSourceParams[source] != 0 {
   208			filter.Source = source // unknown values are ignored rather than matching nothing
   209		}
   210		return filter
   211	}
   212	
   213	func (f notificationFilter) IsActive() bool {
   214		return f.RepoID != 0 || f.Source != ""
   215	}
   216	
   217	func (f notificationFilter) findOptions(userID int64) activities_model.FindNotificationOptions {
   218		opts := activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: userID, RepoID: f.RepoID}
   219		if f.Source != "" {
   220			opts.Source = []activities_model.NotificationSource{notificationSourceParams[f.Source]}
   221		}
   222		return opts
   223	}
   224	
   225	// queryString is built from the parsed values, never the raw request, so redirects only carry validated input
   226	func (f notificationFilter) queryString() string {
   227		q := url.Values{}
   228		if f.RepoID != 0 {
   229			q.Set("repo", strconv.FormatInt(f.RepoID, 10))
   230		}
   231		if f.Source != "" {
   232			q.Set("source", f.Source)
   233		}
   234		return q.Encode()
   235	}
   236	
   237	// loadNotificationFilterRepos returns the repositories offered by the repository filter, sorted by full name,
   238	// and the IDs of those with unread notifications
   239	func loadNotificationFilterRepos(ctx stdCtx.Context, doer *user_model.User) (repo_model.RepositoryList, container.Set[int64], error) {
   240		searchOpts := repo_model.SearchRepoOptions{
   241			Actor:   doer,
   242			OwnerID: doer.ID,
   243			Private: true,
   244		}
   245		repos, _, err := repo_model.SearchRepositoryByCondition(ctx, searchOpts, repo_model.SearchRepositoryCondition(searchOpts), false)
   246		if err != nil {
   247			return nil, nil, err
   248		}
   249	
   250		// watched repos the user neither owns nor collaborates on are missing from the search
   251		notifRepoIDs, err := activities_model.FindNotificationRepoIDs(ctx, activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: doer.ID})
   252		if err != nil {
   253			return nil, nil, err
   254		}
   255		known := container.SetOf(repos.IDs()...)
   256		missingIDs := slices.DeleteFunc(notifRepoIDs, func(id int64) bool { return known.Contains(id) })
   257		if len(missingIDs) > 0 {
   258			missing, err := repo_model.GetRepositoriesMapByIDs(ctx, missingIDs)
   259			if err != nil {
   260				return nil, nil, err
   261			}
   262			for _, repo := range missing {
   263				perm, err := access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx, repo, doer)
   264				if err != nil {
   265					return nil, nil, err
   266				}
   267				if perm.HasAnyUnitAccessOrPublicAccess() {
   268					repos = append(repos, repo)
   269				}
   270			}
   271		}
   272		slices.SortFunc(repos, func(a, b *repo_model.Repository) int {
   273			return strings.Compare(strings.ToLower(a.FullName()), strings.ToLower(b.FullName()))
   274		})
   275	
   276		unreadIDs, err := activities_model.FindNotificationRepoIDs(ctx, activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{
   277			UserID: doer.ID,
   278			Status: []activities_model.NotificationStatus{activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread},
   279		})
   280		if err != nil {
   281			return nil, nil, err
   282		}
   283		return repos, container.SetOf(unreadIDs...), nil
   284	}

   286	// NotificationStatusPost is a route for changing the status of a notification
   287	func NotificationStatusPost(ctx *context.Context) {
   288		notificationID := ctx.FormInt64("notification_id")
   289		var newStatus activities_model.NotificationStatus
   290		switch ctx.FormString("notification_action") {
   291		case "mark_as_read":
   292			newStatus = activities_model.NotificationStatusRead
   293		case "mark_as_unread":
   294			newStatus = activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread
   295		case "pin":
   296			newStatus = activities_model.NotificationStatusPinned
   297		default:
   298			return // ignore user's invalid input
   299		}
   300		if _, err := activities_model.SetNotificationStatus(ctx, notificationID, ctx.Doer, newStatus); err != nil {
   301			ctx.ServerError("SetNotificationStatus", err)
   302			return
   303		}
   304	
   305		prepareUserNotificationsData(ctx)
   306		if ctx.Written() {
   307			return
   308		}
   309		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplNotificationDiv)
   310	}
   311	
   312	// NotificationPurgePost is a route for 'purging' the list of notifications - marking all unread as read
   313	func NotificationPurgePost(ctx *context.Context) {
   314		filter := parseNotificationFilter(ctx) // only the notifications the user is looking at are marked
   315		err := activities_model.UpdateNotificationStatuses(ctx, ctx.Doer, activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread, activities_model.NotificationStatusRead, filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID))
   316		if err != nil {
   317			ctx.ServerError("UpdateNotificationStatuses", err)
   318			return
   319		}
   320	
   321		redirect := setting.AppSubURL + "/notifications"
   322		if q := filter.queryString(); q != "" {
   323			redirect += "?" + q
   324		}
   325		ctx.Redirect(redirect, http.StatusSeeOther)
   326	}

   328	// NotificationSubscriptions returns the list of subscribed issues
   329	func NotificationSubscriptions(ctx *context.Context) {
   330		page := max(ctx.FormInt("page"), 1)
   331	
   332		sortType := ctx.FormString("sort")
   333		ctx.Data["SortType"] = sortType
   334	
   335		state := ctx.FormString("state")
   336		if !util.SliceContainsString([]string{"all", "open", "closed"}, state, true) {
   337			state = "all"
   338		}
   339	
   340		ctx.Data["State"] = state
   341		// default state filter is "all"
   342		showClosed := optional.None[bool]()
   343		switch state {
   344		case "closed":
   345			showClosed = optional.Some(true)
   346		case "open":
   347			showClosed = optional.Some(false)
   348		}
   349	
   350		issueType := ctx.FormString("issueType")
   351		// default issue type is no filter
   352		issueTypeBool := optional.None[bool]()
   353		switch issueType {
   354		case "issues":
   355			issueTypeBool = optional.Some(false)
   356		case "pulls":
   357			issueTypeBool = optional.Some(true)
   358		}
   359		ctx.Data["IssueType"] = issueType
   360	
   361		var labelIDs []int64
   362		selectedLabels := ctx.FormString("labels")
   363		ctx.Data["Labels"] = selectedLabels
   364		if len(selectedLabels) > 0 && selectedLabels != "0" {
   365			var err error
   366			labelIDs, err = base.StringsToInt64s(strings.Split(selectedLabels, ","))
   367			if err != nil {
   368				ctx.Flash.Error(ctx.Tr("invalid_data", selectedLabels), true)
   369			}
   370		}
   371	
   372		count, err := issues_model.CountIssues(ctx, &issues_model.IssuesOptions{
   373			SubscriberID: ctx.Doer.ID,
   374			IsClosed:     showClosed,
   375			IsPull:       issueTypeBool,
   376			LabelIDs:     labelIDs,
   377		})
   378		if err != nil {
   379			ctx.ServerError("CountIssues", err)
   380			return
   381		}
   382		issues, err := issues_model.Issues(ctx, &issues_model.IssuesOptions{
   383			Paginator: &db.ListOptions{
   384				PageSize: setting.UI.IssuePagingNum,
   385				Page:     page,
   386			},
   387			SubscriberID: ctx.Doer.ID,
   388			SortType:     sortType,
   389			IsClosed:     showClosed,
   390			IsPull:       issueTypeBool,
   391			LabelIDs:     labelIDs,
   392		})
   393		if err != nil {
   394			ctx.ServerError("Issues", err)
   395			return
   396		}
   397	
   398		commitStatuses, lastStatus, err := pull_service.GetIssuesAllCommitStatus(ctx, issues)
   399		if err != nil {
   400			ctx.ServerError("GetIssuesAllCommitStatus", err)
   401			return
   402		}
   403		if !ctx.Repo.Permission.CanRead(unit.TypeActions) {
   404			for key := range commitStatuses {
   405				git_model.CommitStatusesHideActionsURL(ctx, commitStatuses[key])
   406			}
   407		}
   408		ctx.Data["CommitLastStatus"] = lastStatus
   409		ctx.Data["CommitStatuses"] = commitStatuses
   410		ctx.Data["Issues"] = issues
   411		ctx.Data["IssueRefEndNames"], ctx.Data["IssueRefURLs"] = issue_service.GetRefEndNamesAndURLs(issues, "")
   412	
   413		approvalCounts, err := issues.GetApprovalCounts(ctx)
   414		if err != nil {
   415			ctx.ServerError("ApprovalCounts", err)
   416			return
   417		}
   418		ctx.Data["ApprovalCounts"] = func(issueID int64, typ string) int64 {
   419			counts, ok := approvalCounts[issueID]
   420			if !ok || len(counts) == 0 {
   421				return 0
   422			}
   423			reviewTyp := issues_model.ReviewTypeApprove
   424			switch typ {
   425			case "reject":
   426				reviewTyp = issues_model.ReviewTypeReject
   427			case "waiting":
   428				reviewTyp = issues_model.ReviewTypeRequest
   429			}
   430			for _, count := range counts {
   431				if count.Type == reviewTyp {
   432					return count.Count
   433				}
   434			}
   435			return 0
   436		}
   437	
   438		ctx.Data["Status"] = 1
   439		ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("notification.subscriptions")
   440	
   441		// redirect to last page if request page is more than total pages
   442		pager := context.NewPagination(count, setting.UI.IssuePagingNum, page, 5)
   443		if pager.Paginater.Current() < page {
   444			ctx.Redirect(fmt.Sprintf("/notifications/subscriptions?page=%d", pager.Paginater.Current()))
   445			return
   446		}
   447		pager.AddParamFromRequest(ctx.Req)
   448		ctx.Data["Page"] = pager
   449	
   450		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplNotificationSubscriptions)
   451	}

   453	// NotificationWatching returns the list of watching repos
   454	func NotificationWatching(ctx *context.Context) {
   455		page := max(ctx.FormInt("page"), 1)
   456	
   457		keyword := ctx.FormTrim("q")
   458		ctx.Data["Keyword"] = keyword
   459	
   460		var orderBy db.SearchOrderBy
   461		ctx.Data["SortType"] = ctx.FormString("sort")
   462		switch ctx.FormString("sort") {
   463		case "newest":
   464			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByNewest
   465		case "oldest":
   466			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByOldest
   467		case "recentupdate":
   468			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByRecentUpdated
   469		case "leastupdate":
   470			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByLeastUpdated
   471		case "reversealphabetically":
   472			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByAlphabeticallyReverse
   473		case "alphabetically":
   474			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByAlphabetically
   475		case "moststars":
   476			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByStarsReverse
   477		case "feweststars":
   478			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByStars
   479		case "mostforks":
   480			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByForksReverse
   481		case "fewestforks":
   482			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByForks
   483		default:
   484			ctx.Data["SortType"] = "recentupdate"
   485			orderBy = db.SearchOrderByRecentUpdated
   486		}
   487	
   488		archived := ctx.FormOptionalBool("archived")
   489		ctx.Data["IsArchived"] = archived
   490	
   491		fork := ctx.FormOptionalBool("fork")
   492		ctx.Data["IsFork"] = fork
   493	
   494		mirror := ctx.FormOptionalBool("mirror")
   495		ctx.Data["IsMirror"] = mirror
   496	
   497		template := ctx.FormOptionalBool("template")
   498		ctx.Data["IsTemplate"] = template
   499	
   500		private := ctx.FormOptionalBool("private")
   501		ctx.Data["IsPrivate"] = private
   502	
   503		repos, count, err := repo_model.SearchRepository(ctx, repo_model.SearchRepoOptions{
   504			ListOptions: db.ListOptions{
   505				PageSize: setting.UI.User.RepoPagingNum,
   506				Page:     page,
   507			},
   508			Actor:              ctx.Doer,
   509			Keyword:            keyword,
   510			OrderBy:            orderBy,
   511			Private:            ctx.IsSigned,
   512			WatchedByID:        ctx.Doer.ID,
   513			Collaborate:        optional.Some(false),
   514			TopicOnly:          ctx.FormBool("topic"),
   515			IncludeDescription: setting.UI.SearchRepoDescription,
   516			Archived:           archived,
   517			Fork:               fork,
   518			Mirror:             mirror,
   519			Template:           template,
   520			IsPrivate:          private,
   521		})
   522		if err != nil {
   523			ctx.ServerError("SearchRepository", err)
   524			return
   525		}
   526		ctx.Data["Total"] = count
   527		ctx.Data["Repos"] = repos
   528	
   529		// redirect to last page if request page is more than total pages
   530		pager := context.NewPagination(count, setting.UI.User.RepoPagingNum, page, 5)
   531		pager.AddParamFromRequest(ctx.Req)
   532		ctx.Data["Page"] = pager
   533	
   534		ctx.Data["Status"] = 2
   535		ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("notification.watching")
   536	
   537		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplNotificationSubscriptions)
   538	}

   540	// NewAvailable returns the notification counts
   541	func NewAvailable(ctx *context.Context) {
   542		total, err := db.Count[activities_model.Notification](ctx, activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{
   543			UserID: ctx.Doer.ID,
   544			Status: []activities_model.NotificationStatus{activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread},
   545		})
   546		if err != nil {
   547			log.Error("db.Count[activities_model.Notification]", err)
   548			ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, structs.NotificationCount{New: 0})
   549			return
   550		}
   551	
   552		ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, structs.NotificationCount{New: total})
   553	}

     8	async function receiveUpdateCount(event: MessageEvent<{type: string, data: string}>) {
     9	  try {
    10	    const data = JSON.parse(event.data.data);
    11	    for (const count of document.querySelectorAll('.notification_count')) {
    12	      count.classList.toggle('tw-hidden', data.Count === 0);

    21	export function initNotificationCount() {
    22	  if (!document.querySelector('.notification_count')) return;
    23	
    24	  let usingPeriodicPoller = false;
    25	  const startPeriodicPoller = (timeout: number, lastCount?: number) => {
    26	    if (timeout <= 0 || !Number.isFinite(timeout)) return;
    27	    usingPeriodicPoller = true;
    28	    lastCount = lastCount ?? getCurrentCount();
    29	    setTimeout(async () => {
    30	      await updateNotificationCountWithCallback(startPeriodicPoller, timeout, lastCount);
    31	    }, timeout);
    32	  };
    33	
    34	  if (notificationSettings.EventSourceUpdateTime > 0 && window.EventSource && window.SharedWorker) {
    35	    // Try to connect to the event source via the shared worker first
    36	    const worker = new UserEventsSharedWorker('notification-worker');
    37	    worker.addMessageEventListener((event: MessageEvent) => {
    38	      if (event.data.type === 'no-event-source') {
    39	        if (!usingPeriodicPoller) startPeriodicPoller(notificationSettings.MinTimeout);
    40	      } else if (event.data.type === 'notification-count') {
    41	        receiveUpdateCount(event); // no await
    42	      }
    43	    });
    44	    worker.startPort();
    45	    return;
    46	  }
    47	
    48	  startPeriodicPoller(notificationSettings.MinTimeout);
    49	}

    55	async function updateNotificationCountWithCallback(callback: (timeout: number, newCount: number) => void, timeout: number, lastCount: number) {
    56	  const currentCount = getCurrentCount();
    57	  if (lastCount !== currentCount) {
    58	    callback(notificationSettings.MinTimeout, currentCount);
    59	    return;
    60	  }
    61	
    62	  const newCount = await updateNotificationCount();
    63	  let needsUpdate = false;
    64	
    65	  if (lastCount !== newCount) {
    66	    needsUpdate = true;
    67	    timeout = notificationSettings.MinTimeout;
    68	  } else if (timeout < notificationSettings.MaxTimeout) {
    69	    timeout += notificationSettings.TimeoutStep;
    70	  }
    71	
    72	  callback(timeout, newCount);
    73	  if (needsUpdate) {
    74	    await updateNotificationTable();
    75	  }
    76	}
    77	
    78	async function updateNotificationTable() {
    79	  const notificationDiv = document.querySelector('#notification_div');
    80	  if (!notificationDiv) return;
    81	
    82	  try {
    83	    const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    84	    params.set('div-only', 'true');
    85	    params.set('sequence-number', String(++notificationSequenceNumber));
    86	    const response = await GET(`${appSubUrl}/notifications?${params.toString()}`);
    87	
    88	    if (!response.ok) {
    89	      throw new Error('Failed to fetch notification table');
    90	    }
    91	
    92	    const data = await response.text();
    93	    const el = createElementFromHTML(data);
    94	    if (parseInt(el.getAttribute('data-sequence-number')!) === notificationSequenceNumber) {
    95	      notificationDiv.outerHTML = data;
    96	    }
    97	  } catch (error) {
    98	    console.error(error);
    99	  }
   100	}

   105

   111	
   112	    toggleElem('.notification_count', data.new !== 0);

   118	// CreateRepoTransferNotification creates  notification for the user a repository was transferred to
   119	func CreateRepoTransferNotification(ctx context.Context, doer, newOwner *user_model.User, repo *repo_model.Repository) error {
   120		return db.WithTx(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
   121			var notify []*Notification
   122	
   123			if newOwner.IsOrganization() {
   124				users, err := organization.GetUsersWhoCanCreateOrgRepo(ctx, newOwner.ID)
   125				if err != nil || len(users) == 0 {

   127				}

   132						Status:    NotificationStatusUnread,
   133						UpdatedBy: doer.ID,
   134						Source:    NotificationSourceRepository,
   135					})
   136				}
   137			} else {

   141					Status:    NotificationStatusUnread,
   142					UpdatedBy: doer.ID,
   143					Source:    NotificationSourceRepository,
   144				}}
   145			}

   170	func updateIssueNotification(ctx context.Context, userID, issueID, commentID, updatedByID int64) error {
   171		notification, err := GetIssueNotification(ctx, userID, issueID)
   172		if err != nil {
   173			return err
   174		}
   175	
   176		// NOTICE: Only update comment id when the before notification on this issue is read, otherwise you may miss some old comments.
   177		// But we need update update_by so that the notification will be reorder
   178		var cols []string
   179		if notification.Status == NotificationStatusRead {
   180			notification.Status = NotificationStatusUnread
   181			notification.CommentID = commentID
   182			cols = []string{"status", "update_by", "comment_id"}
   183		} else {
   184			notification.UpdatedBy = updatedByID
   185			cols = []string{"update_by"}
   186		}
   187	
   188		_, err = db.GetEngine(ctx).ID(notification.ID).Cols(cols...).Update(notification)
   189		return err
   190	}

   329	// GetUIDsAndNotificationCounts returns the unread counts for every user between the two provided times.
   330	// It must return all user IDs which appear during the period, including count=0 for users who have read all.
   331	func GetUIDsAndNotificationCounts(ctx context.Context, since, until timeutil.TimeStamp) ([]UserIDCount, error) {
   332		sql := `SELECT user_id, sum(case when status= ? then 1 else 0 end) AS count FROM notification ` +
   333			`WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM notification WHERE updated_unix >= ? AND ` +
   334			`updated_unix < ?) GROUP BY user_id`
   335		var res []UserIDCount
   336		return res, db.GetEngine(ctx).SQL(sql, NotificationStatusUnread, since, until).Find(&res)
   337	}

   410	// UpdateNotificationStatuses updates the statuses of all of a user's notifications that are of the currentStatus type to the desiredStatus.
   411	// filter narrows the update (e.g. RepoID, Source); its UserID and Status are always overwritten.
   412	func UpdateNotificationStatuses(ctx context.Context, user *user_model.User, currentStatus, desiredStatus NotificationStatus, filter FindNotificationOptions) error {
   413		filter.UserID = user.ID // never let a caller widen the update to another user
   414		filter.Status = []NotificationStatus{currentStatus}
   415		n := &Notification{Status: desiredStatus, UpdatedBy: user.ID}
   416		_, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).
   417			Where(filter.ToConds()).
   418			Cols("status", "updated_by", "updated_unix").
   419			Update(n)
   420		return err
   421	}

   426		return repoIDs, db.GetEngine(ctx).Table("notification").
   427			Where(opts.ToConds()).
   428			Distinct("notification.repo_id").
   429			Find(&repoIDs)

     7		"context"

    22	// FindNotificationOptions represent the filters for notifications. If an ID is 0 it will be ignored.
    23	type FindNotificationOptions struct {
    24		db.ListOptions
    25		UserID            int64
    26		RepoID            int64
    27		IssueID           int64
    28		Status            []NotificationStatus
    29		Source            []NotificationSource
    30		UpdatedAfterUnix  int64
    31		UpdatedBeforeUnix int64
    32	}
    33	
    34	// ToCond will convert each condition into a xorm-Cond
    35	func (opts FindNotificationOptions) ToConds() builder.Cond {
    36		cond := builder.NewCond()
    37		if opts.UserID != 0 {
    38			cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.user_id": opts.UserID})
    39		}
    40		if opts.RepoID != 0 {
    41			cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.repo_id": opts.RepoID})
    42		}
    43		if opts.IssueID != 0 {
    44			cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.issue_id": opts.IssueID})
    45		}
    46		if len(opts.Status) > 0 {
    47			if len(opts.Status) == 1 {
    48				cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.status": opts.Status[0]})
    49			} else {
    50				cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.status", opts.Status))
    51			}
    52		}
    53		if len(opts.Source) > 0 {
    54			cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.source", opts.Source))
    55		}
    56		if opts.UpdatedAfterUnix != 0 {
    57			cond = cond.And(builder.Gte{"notification.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedAfterUnix})
    58		}
    59		if opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix != 0 {
    60			cond = cond.And(builder.Lte{"notification.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix})
    61		}
    62		return cond
    63	}
    64	
    65	func (opts FindNotificationOptions) ToOrders() string {
    66		return "notification.updated_unix DESC"
    67	}

    69	// CreateOrUpdateIssueNotifications creates an issue notification
    70	// for each watcher, or updates it if already exists
    71	// receiverID > 0 just send to receiver, else send to all watcher
    72	func CreateOrUpdateIssueNotifications(ctx context.Context, issueID, commentID, notificationAuthorID, receiverID int64) error {
    73		return db.WithTx(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
    74			return createOrUpdateIssueNotifications(ctx, issueID, commentID, notificationAuthorID, receiverID)

    78	func createOrUpdateIssueNotifications(ctx context.Context, issueID, commentID, notificationAuthorID, receiverID int64) error {
    79		// init
    80		var toNotify container.Set[int64]
    81		notifications, err := db.Find[Notification](ctx, FindNotificationOptions{
    82			IssueID: issueID,
    83		})
    84		if err != nil {
    85			return err
    86		}
    87	
    88		issue, err := issues_model.GetIssueByID(ctx, issueID)
    89		if err != nil {
    90			return err
    91		}
    92	
    93		if receiverID > 0 {
    94			toNotify = make(container.Set[int64], 1)
    95			toNotify.Add(receiverID)
    96		} else {
    97			toNotify = make(container.Set[int64], 32)
    98			issueWatches, err := issues_model.GetIssueWatchersIDs(ctx, issueID, true)
    99			if err != nil {
   100				return err
   101			}
   102			toNotify.AddMultiple(issueWatches...)
   103			if !(issue.IsPull && issues_model.HasWorkInProgressPrefix(issue.Title)) {
   104				repoWatches, err := repo_model.GetRepoWatchersIDs(ctx, issue.RepoID)
   105				if err != nil {
   106					return err
   107				}
   108				toNotify.AddMultiple(repoWatches...)
   109			}
   110			issueParticipants, err := issue.GetParticipantIDsByIssue(ctx)
   111			if err != nil {
   112				return err
   113			}
   114			toNotify.AddMultiple(issueParticipants...)
   115	
   116			// don't notify user who cause notification
   117			delete(toNotify, notificationAuthorID)
   118			// explicit unwatch on issue
   119			issueUnWatches, err := issues_model.GetIssueWatchersIDs(ctx, issueID, false)
   120			if err != nil {
   121				return err
   122			}
   123			for _, id := range issueUnWatches {
   124				toNotify.Remove(id)
   125			}
   126		}
   127	
   128		err = issue.LoadRepo(ctx)
   129		if err != nil {
   130			return err
   131		}
   132	
   133		// notify
   134		for userID := range toNotify {
   135			issue.Repo.Units = nil
   136			user, err := user_model.GetUserByID(ctx, userID)
   137			if err != nil {
   138				if user_model.IsErrUserNotExist(err) {
   139					continue
   140				}
   141	
   142				return err
   143			}
   144			if issue.IsPull && !access_model.CheckRepoUnitUser(ctx, issue.Repo, user, unit.TypePullRequests) {
   145				continue
   146			}
   147			if !issue.IsPull && !access_model.CheckRepoUnitUser(ctx, issue.Repo, user, unit.TypeIssues) {
   148				continue
   149			}
   150	
   151			if notificationExists(notifications, issue.ID, userID) {
   152				if err = updateIssueNotification(ctx, userID, issue.ID, commentID, notificationAuthorID); err != nil {
   153					return err
   154				}
   155				continue
   156			}
   157			if err = createIssueNotification(ctx, userID, issue, commentID, notificationAuthorID); err != nil {
   158				return err
   159			}
   160		}
   161		return nil
   162	}

    24	      </div>
    25	    </div>

    27	}
    28	
    29	export function confirmModal(modal: HTMLElement | ConfirmModalOptions): Promise<boolean> {
    30	  if (!(modal instanceof HTMLElement)) modal = createConfirmModal(modal);
    31	  // hide existing toasts when we need to show a new modal, otherwise the toasts only interfere the UI
    32	  // it's fine to do so because the modal is triggered by user's explicit action, so the user should already have read the toast messages
    33	  hideToastsAll();
    34	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    35	    showFomanticModal(modal, {
    36	      onApprove() {
    37	        resolve(true);
    38	      },
    39	      onHidden() {
    40	        modal.remove();
    41	        resolve(false);
    42	      },
    43	    });
    44	  });

     7	export function request(url: string, {method = 'GET', data, headers = {}, ...other}: RequestOpts = {}): Promise<Response> {
     8	  let body: string | FormData | URLSearchParams | undefined;
     9	  let contentType: string | undefined;
    10	  if (data instanceof FormData || data instanceof URLSearchParams) {
    11	    body = data;

    14	    body = JSON.stringify(data);

    16	
    17	  headers = new Headers(headers);
    18	  if (!headers.has('content-type') && contentType) {
    19	    headers.set('content-type', contentType);
    20	  }
    21	  return fetch(url, { // eslint-disable-line no-restricted-globals
    22	    method,
    23	    headers,
    24	    ...other,
    25	    ...(body && {body}),
    26	  });
    27	}

```text
## Current sprint: Sprint 1

- **Dates:** Sep 22 – Oct 8, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 8, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100 (10% of the course grade).
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D6) or no release (D7) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** every Sprint 0 standard and convention still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 1` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue | 7 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs | 36 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 7 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint1/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint1/report.md` |
| D7 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s1` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D8 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Every issue has exactly **one** assignee. Specs should be final by
  Sep 27.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. The folder must exist even if no AI was used. In
  that case, post an issue comment saying so. Log links go in **issue comments only**, never in PRs
  (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D7:** keep Sprint 0's base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s0` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s1`), push the tag
  to origin, and write release notes listing the features, fixes and improvements.
- **Reviews:** each student reviews at least one PR per sprint. Over the semester, each student
  reviews every teammate at least once.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR accepted by upstream Gitea.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

function buildFetchActionUrl(el: HTMLElement, opt: FetchActionOpts) {
  let url = opt.url;
  if ('name' in el && 'value' in el) {
    // ref: https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-get/
    // If the element with the hx-get attribute also has a value, this will be included as a parameter
    const name = (el as HTMLInputElement).name;
    const val = (el as HTMLInputElement).value;
    const u = new URL(url, window.location.href);
    if (name && !u.searchParams.has(name)) {
      u.searchParams.set(name, val);
      url = u.href;
    }
  }
  return url;
}

async function performActionRequest(el: HTMLElement, opt: FetchActionOpts) {
  const attrIsLoading = 'data-fetch-is-loading';
  if (el.getAttribute(attrIsLoading)) return;
  if (!await confirmFetchAction(opt.formSubmitter ?? el)) return;

  el.setAttribute(attrIsLoading, 'true');
  toggleLoadingIndicator(el, opt, true);

  try {
    const url = buildFetchActionUrl(el, opt);
    const headers = new Headers(opt.headers);
    headers.set('X-Gitea-Fetch-Action', '1');
    const resp = await request(url, {method: opt.method, body: opt.body, headers});
    if (resp.ok) {
      await handleFetchActionSuccess(el, opt, resp);
      return;
    }
    await handleFetchActionError(resp);
  // * data-fetch-trigger: the event to trigger the fetch action, can be:
  //   * "click", "change" (user-initiated events)
  //   * "load" (triggered on page load)
  //   * "every 5s" (also support "ms" unit)
  //   * "fetch-reload" (only triggered by fetch sync success to reload outdated content)
  //
  // * data-fetch-indicator: the loading indicator element selector, it uses the same syntax as "data-fetch-sync" to find the element(s)
  //
  // * data-fetch-sync: when the response is text (html), the pseudo selectors/commands defined in "data-fetch-sync"
  //   will be used to update the content in the current page. It only supports some simple syntaxes that we need.
  //   "$" prefix means it is our private command (for special logic), the selectors are run one by one from current element.
  //   * "$this": replace the current element with the response
  //   * "$innerHTML": replace innerHTML of the current element with the response, instead of replacing the whole element (outerHTML)
  //   * "$morph": use morph algorithm to update the target element
  //   * "$body #the-id .the-class": query the selector one by one from body
  //   * "$closest(tr) td": pseudo command can help to find the target element in a more flexible way
  //
  // * data-modal-confirm: a "confirm modal dialog" will be shown before taking action.
  //   * it can be a string for the content of the modal dialog
  //   * it has "-header" and "-content" variants to set the header and content of the "confirm modal"
  //   * it can refer an existing modal element by "#the-modal-id"

  addDelegatedEventListener<HTMLFormElement, SubmitEvent>(document, 'submit', '.form-fetch-action', async (el, e) => {
    // "fetch-action" will use the form's data to send the request
    e.preventDefault();
    await submitFormFetchAction(el, {formSubmitter: e.submitter});
  });

  addDelegatedEventListener(document, 'click', '.link-action', async (el, e) => {
    // `<a class="link-action" data-url="...">` is a shorthand for
    // `<a data-fetch-trigger="click" data-fetch-method="post" data-fetch-url="..." data-fetch-indicator="$this">`
    e.preventDefault();
    await performLinkFetchAction(el);
  });

  registerGlobalSelectorFunc('[data-fetch-url]', initFetchActionTrigger);

const (
	// NotificationStatusUnread represents an unread notification
	NotificationStatusUnread NotificationStatus = iota + 1
	// NotificationStatusRead represents a read notification
	NotificationStatusRead
	// NotificationStatusPinned represents a pinned notification
	NotificationStatusPinned
)

const (
func SetNotificationStatus(ctx context.Context, notificationID int64, user *user_model.User, status NotificationStatus) (*Notification, error) {
	notification, err := GetNotificationByID(ctx, notificationID)
	if err != nil {
		return notification, err
	}

	if notification.UserID != user.ID {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("Can't change notification of another user: %d, %d", notification.UserID, user.ID)
	}

	notification.Status = status

	_, err = db.GetEngine(ctx).ID(notificationID).Cols("status").Update(notification)
	return notification, err
}

// GetNotificationByID return notification by ID
func GetNotificationByID(ctx context.Context, notificationID int64) (*Notification, error) {
	notification := new(Notification)
	ok, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).
		Where("id = ?", notificationID).
		Get(notification)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if !ok {
		return nil, db.ErrNotExist{Resource: "notification", ID: notificationID}
	}

	return notification, nil
}

// UpdateNotificationStatuses updates the statuses of all of a user's notifications that are of the currentStatus type to the desiredStatus.
// filter narrows the update (e.g. RepoID, Source); its UserID and Status are always overwritten.
func UpdateNotificationStatuses(ctx context.Context, user *user_model.User, currentStatus, desiredStatus NotificationStatus, filter FindNotificationOptions) error {
	filter.UserID = user.ID // never let a caller widen the update to another user
	filter.Status = []NotificationStatus{currentStatus}
	n := &Notification{Status: desiredStatus, UpdatedBy: user.ID}
	_, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).
		Where(filter.ToConds()).
		Cols("status", "updated_by", "updated_unix").
		Update(n)
	return err
}

// FindNotificationRepoIDs returns the distinct repository IDs of the notifications matching opts
func FindNotificationRepoIDs(ctx context.Context, opts FindNotificationOptions) ([]int64, error) {
===
)

// FindNotificationOptions represent the filters for notifications. If an ID is 0 it will be ignored.
type FindNotificationOptions struct {
	db.ListOptions
	UserID            int64
	RepoID            int64
	IssueID           int64
	Status            []NotificationStatus
	Source            []NotificationSource
	UpdatedAfterUnix  int64
	UpdatedBeforeUnix int64
}

// ToCond will convert each condition into a xorm-Cond
func (opts FindNotificationOptions) ToConds() builder.Cond {
	cond := builder.NewCond()
	if opts.UserID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.user_id": opts.UserID})
	}
	if opts.RepoID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.repo_id": opts.RepoID})
	}
	if opts.IssueID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.issue_id": opts.IssueID})
	}
	if len(opts.Status) > 0 {
		if len(opts.Status) == 1 {
			cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.status": opts.Status[0]})
		} else {
			cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.status", opts.Status))
		}
	}
	if len(opts.Source) > 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.source", opts.Source))
	}
	if opts.UpdatedAfterUnix != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Gte{"notification.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedAfterUnix})
	}
	if opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Lte{"notification.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix})
	}
	return cond
}

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import {login, apiCreateRepo, apiCreateIssue, randomString} from './utils.ts';

test('bulk close selected issues with the reason picked in the menu', async ({page, request}) => {
  const repoName = `e2e-bulk-close-${randomString(8)}`;
  const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
  await apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repoName, autoInit: false});
  await Promise.all([
    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo: repoName, title: 'First bulk close test'}),
    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo: repoName, title: 'Second bulk close test'}),
    login(page),
  ]);
  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repoName}/issues?state=open`);

  await page.locator('.issue-checkbox-all').check();
  const closeGroup = page.locator('#issue-actions [data-global-init="initIssueListCloseReason"]');
  await closeGroup.locator('.ui.dropdown').click();
  await closeGroup.locator('.menu .item', {hasText: 'Not planned'}).click();
  // the button takes the picked reason, and its request carries it; the page reloads once the server answers
  await Promise.all([
    page.waitForResponse((response) => response.url().endsWith('/issues/status')),
    closeGroup.getByRole('button', {name: 'Close as not planned'}).click(),
  ]);

  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repoName}/issues?state=closed`);
  await expect(page.locator('#issue-list .item-leading .octicon-skip')).toHaveCount(2); // not planned's icon, not the red one of no reason
});

func ReadNotifications(ctx *context.APIContext) {
	// swagger:operation PUT /notifications notification notifyReadList
	// ---
	// summary: Mark notification threads as read, pinned or unread
	// consumes:
	// - application/json
	// produces:
	// - application/json
	// parameters:
	// - name: last_read_at
	//   in: query
	//   description: Describes the last point that notifications were checked. Anything updated since this time will not be updated.
	//   type: string
	//   format: date-time
	//   required: false
	// - name: all
	//   in: query
	//   description: If true, mark all notifications on this repo. Default value is false
	//   type: string
	//   required: false
	// - name: status-types
	//   in: query
	//   description: "Mark notifications with the provided status types. Options are: unread, read and/or pinned. Defaults to unread."
	//   type: array
	//   collectionFormat: multi
	//   items:
	//     type: string
	//   required: false
	// - name: to-status
	//   in: query
	//   description: Status to mark notifications as, Defaults to read.
	//   type: string
	//   required: false
	// responses:
	//   "205":
	//     "$ref": "#/responses/NotificationThreadList"

	lastRead := int64(0)
	qLastRead := ctx.FormTrim("last_read_at")
	if len(qLastRead) > 0 {
		tmpLastRead, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, qLastRead)
		if err != nil {
			ctx.APIError(http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
			return
		}
		if !tmpLastRead.IsZero() {
			lastRead = tmpLastRead.Unix()
		}
	}
	opts := &activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{
		UserID:            ctx.Doer.ID,
		UpdatedBeforeUnix: lastRead,
	}
	if !ctx.FormBool("all") {
		statuses := ctx.FormStrings("status-types")
		opts.Status = statusStringsToNotificationStatuses(statuses, []string{"unread"})
	}
	nl, err := db.Find[activities_model.Notification](ctx, opts)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.APIErrorInternal(err)
		return
	}

	targetStatus := statusStringToNotificationStatus(ctx.FormString("to-status"))
	if targetStatus == 0 {
		targetStatus = activities_model.NotificationStatusRead
	}

	changed := make([]*structs.NotificationThread, 0, len(nl))

	for _, n := range nl {
		notif, err := activities_model.SetNotificationStatus(ctx, n.ID, ctx.Doer, targetStatus)
		if err != nil {
			ctx.APIErrorInternal(err)
			return
		}
		_ = notif.LoadAttributes(ctx)
		changed = append(changed, convert.ToNotificationThread(ctx, notif))
	}

	ctx.JSON(http.StatusResetContent, changed)
}

// the markup the Issues tab's toolbar gets while open issues are listed
function createCloseButtons() {
  const elButtons = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(`
    <div class="ui red basic buttons" data-global-init="initIssueListCloseReason">
      <button class="ui button issue-action" data-action="close" data-url="/user2/repo1/issues/status" data-close-reason="completed">Close as completed</button>
      <div class="ui dropdown icon button">
        <div class="menu">
          <div class="item js-aria-clickable selected" data-value="completed" data-status="Close as completed">Completed</div>
          <div class="item js-aria-clickable" data-value="not_planned" data-status="Close as not planned">Not planned</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>`);
  initIssueListCloseReason(elButtons);
  const closeButton = elButtons.querySelector('.issue-action')!;
  const pick = (reason: string) => elButtons.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`.item[data-value="${CSS.escape(reason)}"]`)!.click();
  return {elButtons, closeButton, pick};
}

test('picking a reason gives the Close button that reason and its text', () => {
  const {closeButton, pick} = createCloseButtons();
  pick('not_planned');
  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('not_planned');
  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as not planned');
  pick('completed'); // the reason can still be changed before closing
  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('completed');
  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as completed');
});

test('a click in the menu that misses every item changes nothing', () => {
  const {elButtons, closeButton} = createCloseButtons();
  elButtons.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.menu')!.click();
  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('completed');
  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as completed');
});

# web_src/js — page features and how they get wired up

**Read when:** adding or changing browser behaviour on a page.
**Not here:** Vue components -> `frontend-vue-components.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`; the HTML -> `templates.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `features/` | one file per page or feature (`repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, `repo-code.ts`), plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` for shared widgets |
| `modules/` | cross-cutting infrastructure: `fetch.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `toast.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `codeeditor/` |
| `utils/` | pure helpers with no DOM assumptions: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`, `string.ts` |
| `markup/`, `render/` | enhancing already-rendered content (anchors, mermaid, math) |
| `webcomponents/` | custom elements such as `relative-time`, `overflow-menu` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `web_src/js/index.ts` | the entry point: imports fomantic and `../css/index.css`, then passes every `initXxx` to `callInitFunctions` |
| `web_src/js/modules/init.ts` | `callInitFunctions`, `InitPerformanceTracer` |
| `web_src/js/modules/observer.ts` | `registerGlobalInitFunc`, `registerGlobalEventFunc`, `registerGlobalSelectorFunc`, `initGlobalSelectorObserver` |
| `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` |
| `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` | `showElem`, `hideElem`, `toggleElem`, `queryElems`, `createElementFromHTML` |
| `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` | `trN` — the frontend side of the locale system |

## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**

1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
   and return immediately when they are absent.
2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.

`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already spread across many pages, not
for new work.

- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
  wrapper and query for the inner element.
- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.

## Recipes

**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.

**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.

**Profile a slow page.** Append `?_ui_performance_trace=1` to the URL to print per-init timings.
`index.ts` already logs an error when total init exceeds 500ms.

**Look up an issue by its number.** `matchIssue` (`utils/match.ts`) is the `#` list's search: a
number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), and the current issue
is left out. Keyword matches are limited to the kinds the viewer may read
(`routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`), but the match by number (`GetIssueByIndex`) is not, so a
viewer who can't read pull requests still gets one typed by its number. The duplicate close
reason's preview in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` uses it.

**Run one test file.** `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- Forgetting the early return in a page-load init means that feature's cost is paid on every page
  in Gitea, which is what the 500ms warning is there to catch.
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
  in `modules/` or `features/`.
- A feature can follow a comment box it did not create: the editor's change and upload events
  bubble (`features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`, `features/comp/EditorUpload.ts`), and
  `getComboMarkdownEditor` finds the editor, as `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` does. But
  the editor attaches itself before its async `init` finishes, and calling it before then throws;
  read its textarea until an event arrives.
- Enter on a Fomantic dropdown item only fires a `click` when the item is a link or carries
  `js-aria-clickable` (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`), so a plain click listener on other
  items never hears a keyboard pick. `templates/repo/issue/view_content/context_menu.tmpl` and the
  close reason menu in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl` mark their items.
- After a click on a Fomantic dropdown item, the dropdown keeps the focus, so focusing something
  else from your click handler needs `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
- `createTippy` (`modules/tippy.ts`) moves a popup to `document.body`, so inputs in it leave their
  `<form>` and are not sent. Keep their values in hidden fields inside the form, as the close reason
  popups in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` do.

## Related

- `frontend-vue-components.md` — when a feature should be a Vue app instead
- `templates.md` — where `data-global-init` attributes and `pageData` come from
- `frontend-css.md` — `tw-hidden` and the class conventions
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Read templates and css doc conventions

`cd "C:/Users/carso/Desktop/Classes/Year 4/SEM 1/Software Engineering/Gitea" && export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1; git show "origin/main:.claude-students/docs/templates.md" | sed -n '/## Conventions/,/## Related/p'; echo =====; git show "origin/main:.claude-students/docs/frontend-css.md" | sed -n '/## Conventions/,/## Related/p'`

```text
## Conventions & invariants

- A template is addressed by its path under `templates/` without the extension, as a
  `templates.TplName` constant in the handler — `"repo/issue/list"` is
  `templates/repo/issue/list.tmpl` (`routers-web.md`).
- **The handler's `ctx.Data` is the only data channel.** A template cannot reach anything the
  handler did not put there, and `ctx.RootData` inside a template context is that same data.
- Data destined for JavaScript goes through `ctx.PageData`, which `base/head_script.tmpl` emits as
  `window.config.pageData` — a separate channel from `ctx.Data`.
- **Every user-visible string is a locale key**, written `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.new"}}` or
  `ctx.Locale.TrN` for plurals. Never a literal. Keys are added only to
  `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`; the other locales come from Crowdin.
- Composition is `{{template "base/head" .}}` style includes. New shared markup goes in `shared/`,
  not copied between areas.
- `dict` is lowercase for historical reasons; new template functions get uppercase names
  (`helper.go` says so at the definition).
- `dict` treats the key `"."` specially: `dictMerge` in `modules/templates/util_dict.go` flattens
  that argument's map into the new one. So `dict "." $ "Issues" $subset` hands a partial the whole
  root context with one key replaced — but `"." $` **must come first**, or the merge overwrites the
  replacement instead. `templates/repo/issue/list_grouped.tmpl` renders each group this way.
- Mail templates use a different, smaller function set — `mailBodyFuncMap` and
  `mailSubjectTextFuncMap` in `modules/templates/mail.go`. A helper added for pages is not
  available in `templates/mail/`.
- Class attributes are written as one readable unit including their conditionals
  (`frontend-css.md`).
- Hook frontend behaviour up declaratively with `data-global-init` / `data-global-click`
  attributes rather than inline script (`frontend-js.md`).
- `.tmpl` files are tab-indented (`.editorconfig`).

## Recipes

**Add a page's template.** Create the `.tmpl` under the matching area directory, include
`base/head` and `base/footer`, declare the `TplName` constant in the handler, and add every string
as a locale key.

**Share markup between pages.** Put the partial in `templates/shared/` and include it from both
places. Two near-identical partials in two area directories is the thing to avoid.

**Add a template function.** Add it to the map returned by `newFuncMapWebPage` in
`modules/templates/helper.go` and implement it in the matching `util_*.go`. Prefer passing prepared data from the handler — a function that
does database work at render time is a performance bug.

**See a component in isolation.** Run Gitea in development mode and open `/devtest`.

## Gotchas

- A misspelled key in `ctx.Data` renders as empty, not as an error. Check the handler when
  something is silently blank.
- A missing locale key renders the key itself — visible, but easy to miss in a rarely-hit branch.
- `templates/swagger/v1_json.tmpl` is generated. Edit the swagger comments and run
  `make generate-swagger` instead (`routers-api-v1.md`).
- `templates/custom/` is for deployment overrides, not a place to put course code.

## Related
=====
## Conventions & invariants

- **Tailwind utilities are prefixed `tw-`** (set in `tailwind.config.ts`), so `tw-hidden`,
  `tw-flex`. An unprefixed Tailwind class does nothing.
- Prefer the `flex-*` layout helpers over per-child `tw-ml-*` / `tw-mr-*` margins (`AGENTS.md`).
  Fall back to `tw-*` utilities where specificity forces `!important`.
- Gitea's own helpers live in `helpers.css`: `gt-` for general helpers, `g-` for framework-level
  ones. Use them **only where Tailwind has no utility** — do not add a `gt-` class that duplicates
  a `tw-` one.
- **Never edit a framework class to restyle something.** Create a new class name and apply it
  alongside (`docs/guidelines-frontend.md`).
- Avoid `!important`; where it is unavoidable, leave a comment saying why. The existing `gt-`
  helpers use it deliberately, which is why they win over framework rules.
- Class and id names are kebab-case with two or three feature keywords, prefixed to avoid
  collisions between frameworks.
- In a template, write the class attribute as one readable unit rather than concatenating:

  ```html
  <div class="flex-text-inline {{if .IsFoo}}tw-hidden{{end}}"></div>
  ```

- `tw-hidden` is also the show/hide mechanism used by `showElem`/`hideElem` in
  `frontend-js.md` — do not reuse it as a generic styling class.

## Recipes

**Style a new feature.** Add `web_src/css/features/<name>.css`, import it from `index.css`, and use
a `.<feature>-` class prefix so the names cannot collide.

**Restyle a Fomantic component.** Look in `web_src/css/modules/` first — many components are
already replaced there, and the replacement is the file to change.

**Add a theme-aware colour.** Use the variables from `themes/`, never a literal colour, or the
other themes break.

**Add a colour theme.** Drop a `web_src/css/themes/theme-<name>.css`. The glob in
`vite.config.ts` makes every file there its own build entry and `services/webtheme` discovers it by
filename, so there is nothing else to register — no Go, template or `app.ini` change. The file must
carry its own `gitea-theme-meta-info` block, because the backend parses the *last* one in the built
output; the cheapest shape imports the matching stock theme and overrides only what the palette
changes:

```css
@import "./theme-gitea-dark.css";

gitea-theme-meta-info {
  --theme-display-name: "Nord Dark";
  --theme-color-scheme: "dark";
}

:root { --color-primary: #81a1c1; }
```

Import the theme matching your scheme: it supplies `--is-dark-theme`, `color-scheme` and the
`var()`-derived colours, which is why `--color-primary-hover` and friends must be left alone.
`web_src/js/utils/theme-files.test.ts` then checks every theme's meta block and its contrast
against the stock theme it extends.

## Gotchas

- Forgetting the `@import` in `index.css` means your file compiles to nothing, with no error.
- The Tailwind `content` globs in `tailwind.config.ts` decide which classes survive the build. A
  class assembled dynamically in JavaScript will be purged — write the full class name literally.
- `tailwind.config.ts` has a `blocklist`; a utility that mysteriously does not exist may be listed
  there on purpose.
- `web_src/css/modules/` is Gitea's *replacement* for Fomantic, not Fomantic itself — the vendored
  original is under `web_src/fomantic/`.
- A theme file must not introduce a *new* `--color-*` name. `tailwind.config.ts` and
  `stylelint.config.ts` read only `base.css` and the two `theme-gitea-*` files, so an unknown name
  fails `make lint-css` and never gets a `tw-` utility.
- A Fomantic dropdown's menu is a child of the dropdown, so any ancestor with `overflow: hidden`
  cuts it off: the menu opens but cannot be seen. Tippy popups (`web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts`) are
  attached to `document.body` and are never cut off.
- Below 768px, `repo.css` makes every button in an issue's comment form full-width, buttons inside
  a `ui buttons` group included. Group buttons cannot shrink, so a group needs its own sizing there,
  as the close button's group has, or its ▾ spills over the Comment button.

    24	  let usingPeriodicPoller = false;
    25	  const startPeriodicPoller = (timeout: number, lastCount?: number) => {
    26	    if (timeout <= 0 || !Number.isFinite(timeout)) return;
    27	    usingPeriodicPoller = true;
    28	    lastCount = lastCount ?? getCurrentCount();
    29	    setTimeout(async () => {

    33

    35	    // Try to connect to the event source via the shared worker first
    36	    const worker = new UserEventsSharedWorker('notification-worker');
    37	    worker.addMessageEventListener((event: MessageEvent) => {
    38	      if (event.data.type === 'no-event-source') {
    39	        if (!usingPeriodicPoller) startPeriodicPoller(notificationSettings.MinTimeout);
    40	      } else if (event.data.type === 'notification-count') {
    41	        receiveUpdateCount(event); // no await

    43	    });
    44	    worker.startPort();

    46	  }
    47	
    48	  startPeriodicPoller(notificationSettings.MinTimeout);

    55	async function updateNotificationCountWithCallback(callback: (timeout: number, newCount: number) => void, timeout: number, lastCount: number) {
    56	  const currentCount = getCurrentCount();
    57	  if (lastCount !== currentCount) {
    58	    callback(notificationSettings.MinTimeout, currentCount);
    59	    return;
    60	  }
    61

    66	    needsUpdate = true;
    67	    timeout = notificationSettings.MinTimeout;
    68	  } else if (timeout < notificationSettings.MaxTimeout) {
    69	    timeout += notificationSettings.TimeoutStep;
    70	  }

    72	  callback(timeout, newCount);
